videos.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
videos.description: Michael Portillo's nineteenth-century Appleton's guidebook leads him to the Parker House Hotel, where in his best pinny, he whisks up a Boston cream pie. In the fine dome atop Massachusetts General Hospital, where no-one could hear the screaming, Michael discovers the scene of grisly surgery, first made bearable, in 1846, by a miraculous new substance. North of Boston, in Salem, Michael is caught up in a witch hunt.

videos.title: Saving Lives at Sea
videos.description: On the North Somerset coast, the Minehead crew come close to disaster in a challenging rescue of two walkers cut off by the tide. Plus, in Dunbar a boy has fallen from some notoriously dangerous rocks and suffered a potentially life-changing injury.

videos.title: Fred Dibnah's Age of Steam
videos.description: Part 3/6. Fred explores the extraordinary role of steam in the expansion of industrial Britain. Along the way, Fred learns how huge stationary steam engines continued to be used in mills, collieries and steel works until well into the 20th century.

videos.title: Fred Dibnah's Age of Steam
videos.description: Part 4/6. Fred Dibnah looks at early experiments in the use of steam power for road transportation. Along the way, Fred explores the development of the traction engine and its use in both agriculture and haulage.

videos.title: Fred Dibnah's Age of Steam
videos.description: Part 5/6. Fred Dibnah has a look at how steam power had a revolutionary impact on shipping. In the process, Fred explores vessels ranging from early paddle steamers to the Royal Yacht Britannia.

videos.title: Fred Dibnah's Age of Steam
videos.description: Fred explores how steam power lives on in the modern age through the steam turbine and its critical role in electricity generation. In addition, Fred also looks at how the history of steam is being preserved through heritage museums.

videos.title: Train Rescue Down Under
videos.description: The maintenance crews test pantographs, repair faulty air conditioning units and clear debris from overhead high voltage train power lines.

videos.title: Martin Clunes Islands of Australia
videos.description: Exploring Lord Howe Island, Norfolk Island and Restoration Island; Thursday and Friday Islands, the homes of music and pearls.

videos.title: Martin Clunes Islands of Australia
videos.description: Martin Clunes travels to the Tiwi Islands, swims with a whale shark, visits the Houtman Abrolhos, a string of over 100 tiny islands, and samples life on Rottnest Island.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: Life on board a narrowboat with Robbie Cumming. There are engine issues and a leaky boat to fix before Robbie reaches Liverpool Docks.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: Life on board a narrowboat with Robbie Cumming. Robbie battles his way through blanket weed on the Shropshire Union Canal and accidentally floods a staircase lock in Chester.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: Robbie gets stuck in the mud in Woodseaves Cutting and explores the charming canal-side village of Kinver in Staffordshire.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: Robbie navigates the mighty River Severn and takes an unexpected bath as he tumbles at the Tardebigge lock flight in Worcestershire.

videos.title: Bill Bailey's Jungle Hero
videos.description: Comedian Bill Bailey ventures to Indonesia's remote Spice Islands, in the footsteps of his hero - Victorian naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace. In the second of this two-part series, Bill encounters boggle-eyed tarsiers, monkeys with mohicans and spectacular birds of paradise on his mission to understand how Wallace cracked evolution.

videos.title: The Green Planet
videos.description: Deserts are hostile: temperatures soar, and water is rare. Desert plants spend decades in suspended animation waiting for rain, or they travel to find it. They survive using weapons, camouflage, and surprising alliances with animals.

videos.title: The Green Planet
videos.description: We rely on plants for almost everything, including the air we breathe and the food we eat. Two in five wild plants are threatened with extinction, but people are finding new ways to help them, from projects in Africa to reseed the landscape to the rebuilding of a tropical forest in Brazil, tree by tree.

videos.title: Bangers & Cash: Restoring Classics
videos.description: The team invest in a piece of French art this week: a 1971 Citroën DS21 Pallas.

videos.title: Bangers & Cash: Restoring Classics
videos.description: This week tells the tale of the two Mercs, but what will the moral of the story be? Plus, the team get stuck into a moddable favourite - a 2006 Ford Fiesta ST.

videos.title: Bangers & Cash: Restoring Classics
videos.description: The team seek out a sturdy, reliable 4x4 to tackle the rugged Yorkshire landscape in, but get side-tracked into a slightly rusty Subaru Impreza Turbo 2000.

videos.title: Yes, Minister
videos.description: The minister is shocked to discover that his department is responsible for supplying all the Government's electronic surveillance equipment.

videos.title: Yes, Minister
videos.description: Jim Hacker finds himself in the middle of a major row over the British Chemical Corporation, and Sir Humphrey tries to get Jim to support the politically unpopular measure.

videos.title: Yes, Minister
videos.description: Jim Hacker is upset by rumours of a cabinet reshuffle and decides to take drastic action to keep his post.

videos.title: War's Secret Shame - Shell Shock
videos.description: Dan Snow investigates a century of war trauma from WW1 shell shock to modern PTSD. For 100 years, men and women who risked their lives for their country have continued to suffer on their return.

videos.title: Bangers and Cash
videos.description: Derek's search for the unusual leads him to a 1947 Lea Francis that is half wood, Paul picks up a Morris truck out in the countryside, and Dave takes care of an iconic Italian Alfasud.

videos.title: Great British Railway Journeys
videos.description: Michael Portillo explores the post-war Britain of his youth in a journey from the Midlands to the West Country. Beginning in Derby's railway works, Michael hears how the Victorian sheds now house some of the most modern assembly lines in Britain.

videos.title: Teleshopping
videos.description: Presenting the latest products live on television that can be ordered directly. The product range extends from vacuum cleaners and bath towels to sports equipment.

videos.title: Great British Railway Journeys
videos.description: Michael Portillo is in Crewe, a town steeped in railway history and immortalised in Victorian music hall, to investigate the making of the iconic cinema classic The Night Mail during the 1930s.

videos.title: Great British Railway Journeys
videos.description: In Coventry, Michael recalls the destruction by the German Luftwaffe of the city's gothic cathedral in November 1940. Heading south to Royal Leamington Spa, Michael visits the Guide Dogs for the Blind National Centre, established in the town in 1941.

videos.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
videos.description: Guided by his Appleton's and tracing the footsteps of the Pilgrim Fathers, Michael Portillo heads for Plymouth, the 'home town' of America. He learns how indigenous tribes of Wampanoag people taught newly arrived settlers to live off the land, inspiring one of the biggest holidays in today's American calendar.

videos.title: Fred Dibnah's Made in Britain
videos.description: Fred reaches Cumbria where iron ore was once mined on a large scale, and enjoys the Lake District on a friend's steam boat and it's then on to the Florence Mine at Egremont and the Workington Steel Works.

videos.title: Fred Dibnah's Made in Britain
videos.description: Fred and his steersman Alf travel up to Scotland where they marvel at the ingenuity of the Falkirk wheel and visit one of the few surviving traditional iron works left in the region.

videos.title: Fred Dibnah's Made in Britain
videos.description: Fred visits Ryhope pumping station in Sunderland, meets the volunteers who maintain the museum, travels across the Middlesborough transporter bridge and sees the Israel Newton boiler works in Bradford.

videos.title: Fred Dibnah's Made in Britain
videos.description: Fred fulfils his ambition to drive across the imposing Scammonden Bridge over the M62. Fred also visits Sheffield to take a tour around a forge and to watch crucible steel being produced.

videos.title: Martin Clunes Islands of Australia
videos.description: Exploring Lord Howe Island, Norfolk Island and Restoration Island; Thursday and Friday Islands, the homes of music and pearls.

videos.title: Martin Clunes Islands of Australia
videos.description: Martin Clunes travels to the Tiwi Islands, swims with a whale shark, visits the Houtman Abrolhos, a string of over 100 tiny islands, and samples life on Rottnest Island.

videos.title: David Jason's Secret Service
videos.description: Sir David lifts the lid on true stories of unbelievable heroism in World War II and explores a world of cold-blooded assassins, crack saboteurs, elite commandos, real-life super-villains and the ultimate femmes fatales.

videos.title: David Jason's Secret Service
videos.description: Sir David finds out how the best brains in Britain were recruited to help win a very secret war. From high-tech intelligence to undercover ops, he reveals how the real Qs of World War II defeated Hitler with their ingenious problem-solving designs.

videos.title: Operation Arctic with Simon Reeve
videos.description: The team discover why the Arctic is changing faster than anywhere else on Earth. In a place where life is driven by ice, we see what happens when it disappears.

videos.title: This World
videos.description: Part 2/2. Adventurer and journalist Simon Reeve heads to Vietnam to uncover the stories behind the nation's morning pick-me-up. While we drink millions of cups of the stuff each week, how many of us know where our coffee actually comes from?

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: The real side of boating with Robbie Cumming. On the last leg of his epic journey across the North of England, Robbie tackles the fast-flowing River Ouse and is forced to make an emergency stop. His destination is Ripon Basin at the outer reaches of our inland waterways.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: Robbie Cumming begins his 300-mile boating adventure across the north of England and the Midlands. He is forced to make a running repair to his narrowboat, the Naughty Lass, while on the Tinsley lock flight in South Yorkshire, he cruises beneath Conisbrough's magnificent viaduct and must wait for an unusual sliding railway bridge to open on the Stainforth and Keadby Canal.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: Robbie Cumming tackles the fast-flowing tidal River Trent and is invited to join a night-time illuminated boat parade. However, his journey is hampered by a damaged wall in Worksop and a water shortage on the picturesque Chesterfield Canal.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: Autumnal fog and an overheating engine prove to be problems for narrowboater Robbie Cumming as he navigates a Roman waterway and the fast-flowing River Trent. It's a journey of many challenges as he runs aground and breaks down in Nottingham.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: Robbie takes a detour to investigate a local UFO legend in Todmorden, and the UK's deepest canal lock springs a leak, causing trouble for the Naughty Lass.

videos.title: Canal Boat Diaries
videos.description: Robbie Cumming journeys through Royal Leamington Spa and the historic town of Warwick with its medieval castle.

videos.description: The team invest in a piece of French art this week: a 1971 Citroën DS21 Pallas.

videos.title: Bangers & Cash: Restoring Classics
videos.description: This week tells the tale of the two Mercs, but what will the moral of the story be? Plus, the team get stuck into a moddable favourite - a 2006 Ford Fiesta ST.

videos.title: Bangers and Cash
videos.description: Dave heads to Bolton to pick up a classic Italian sports car - a Lancia Fulvia 1.3 Sport. This classic car was styled by the well known Milanese coach builder, Zagato. Zagato is famous for collaborating with high-end car brands.

videos.title: Bangers and Cash
videos.description: Derek rubs shoulders with pop music royalty when he picks up a classic Morgan sports car. A World War Two ambulance arrives at Thornton le Dale and a Ford Model T needs a new home.

videos.title: Bangers and Cash
videos.description: Dave and Jack head for East Yorkshire to collect a dusty Alfa Romeo and a 1930s Jowett, but Dave is more interested in a possible Christmas present. Meanwhile, a VW Beetle and a Renault 5 GT turbo get pulses racing.

videos.title: Bangers and Cash
videos.description: Derek picks up a lovingly restored 1925 Calthorpe motorbike that he thinks is more of a work of art than anything ever produced by Picasso.

videos.title: Great British Railway Journeys
videos.description: Michael Portillo is in Crewe, a town steeped in railway history and immortalised in Victorian music hall, to investigate the making of the iconic cinema classic The Night Mail during the 1930s.

videos.title: Great British Railway Journeys

videos.title: Great British Railway Journeys
videos.description: Michael Portillo's 1930s Bradshaw's-inspired railway tour of north Wales takes him to a coast lined by magnificent castles and sweeping bays. In Colwyn Bay, he hears how an army of civil servants invaded the quiet seaside town.

videos.title: Great British Railway Journeys
videos.description: Michael Portillo's railway journey reaches the heart of Warwickshire. In the Tudor town of Stratford-upon-Avon, birthplace of William Shakespeare, Michael visits the Royal Shakespeare Theatre, home since 1961 to the Royal Shakespeare Company.

videos.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
videos.description: Armed with his Appleton's guide, Michael Portillo continues his rail journey through Connecticut and New England. He takes a crash course in rowing in New Haven, where college teams from Yale and Harvard have battled for victory on the water since 1852. In Vermont, Michael visits a 19th-century farm, where the rich milk from prized Jersey cows imported from the British Isles supplied a thriving butter industry.

videos.title: Bangers and Cash
videos.description: Derek meets the owner and builder of a sporty vintage Jaguar 'special', a Jaguar Viking.

videos.title: Bangers & Cash: Restoring Classics
videos.description: The team take on a modern-day fast Ford to see if a 'quick flip' could make a few quid and revisit a 3-year MG restoration project that's still not finished.

videos.title: The World at War
videos.description: Auschwitz survivors and Himmler's SS adjutant contribute to this harrowing account of the most chilling and inhuman chapter of WWII.

videos.title: Auschwitz: The Nazis and the Final Solution
videos.description: The German occupation of Hungary leads to the deportation of Jews living there. The Western Allies debate whether to bomb the camp. More people are murdered at Auschwitz in 1944, than in all previous years.

videos.title: Antiques Roadshow
videos.description: Antiques Roadshow comes from the lush surroundings of the National Botanic Garden of Wales in Carmarthenshire, where Fiona Bruce discovers how plant-based remedies were mixed and bottled by Victorian pharmacists. Braving the rainy weather, visitors bring an eclectic range of items for the experts to appraise. James Bond memorabilia make an appearance alongside a miniature steam engine and a rare religious ring.

videos.title: Antiques Roadshow
videos.description: Fiona Bruce presents a special episode of Antiques Roadshow commemorating the 80th anniversary of the Battle of Britain and the Blitz. Combining stories from all over the country with a special event filmed at Biggin Hill airfield, the programme tells the story of a defining moment in Britain's war through the people and objects who were there. Fiona begins the programme onboard an iconic Supermarine Spitfire, flying over the Weald of Kent.

videos.title: Bangers and Cash
videos.description: Derek heads to Scotland during a large rainstorm to pick up a Jaguar E-type and a rare MGC convertible, meanwhile Dave extracts a rare Austin Gipsy from a lock-up.

videos.title: Bangers and Cash
videos.description: There's a surprise waiting for Derek in Hull, an MGA sports car that once had a tree growing through it. Plus, in North Wales, Alan Holmes is selling his son's Ford Escort RS 1600i.

videos.description: Michael begins a journey across the Balkan countries of Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Armed with shield and sword and weighed down by a heavy helmet, he mounts a valiant defence against fierce latter-day Roman gladiators in the 2,000-year-old amphitheatre at Pula on Croatia's Istrian peninsula.

videos.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
videos.description: Ably assisted by Lila, an expert Labrador, Michael Portillo hunts for truffles in the Istrian countryside near the hilltop town of Buzet. His railway adventure through the Balkan countries of Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina continues.

videos.title: Simon Reeve's South America
videos.description: Simon travels from Chile's Atacama Desert right down to Tierra Del Fuego, the most southerly inhabited place on Earth. The Atacama, one of the driest places on the planet, has as little as 1mm of rain per year.
